questions.prompt: What is the time complexity of pushing or popping at the ends of a Redis List?

options.text: O(N) — it walks the whole list
O(1) — constant time, regardless of length
O(log N)
It depends on the value size only

questions.explanation: Lists are linked lists, so operations at the head/tail (LPUSH/RPUSH/LPOP/RPOP) are O(1). Indexed middle access (LINDEX) is O(N).

questions.prompt: Which pair of commands implements a FIFO queue?

options.text: LPUSH to add, LPOP to remove
RPUSH to add, LPOP to remove
RPUSH to add, RPOP to remove
SET to add, GET to remove

questions.explanation: For first-in-first-out, push onto the tail (RPUSH) and pop from the head (LPOP). Using the same end (LPUSH+LPOP) gives a LIFO stack.

questions.prompt: Which statements about List commands are true? Select all that apply.

options.text: LTRIM key 0 99 keeps only the first 100 elements
BLPOP blocks until an element is available or the timeout elapses
LMOVE pops from one list and pushes to another atomically
LINDEX on a huge list is O(1)

questions.explanation: LTRIM caps a list, BLPOP blocks efficiently, and LMOVE is an atomic pop-and-push. LINDEX is O(N), not O(1).

questions.prompt: Why prefer BLPOP over an LPOP polling loop for a worker consuming a queue?

options.text: BLPOP can pop multiple keys but LPOP cannot exist
BLPOP waits efficiently for an item instead of repeatedly checking an empty queue
BLPOP guarantees the job is never removed
LPOP is not allowed in production

questions.explanation: BLPOP blocks until work arrives (up to a timeout), avoiding the wasted CPU and round trips of polling an empty list with LPOP.

questions.prompt: To keep a list capped at its most recent 100 items after LPUSH, you run LTRIM key 0 ______. (a number)
questions.explanation: LTRIM key 0 99 keeps indexes 0 through 99 — 100 elements — and discards the rest.

questions.prompt: Which problem does LMOVE (or BLMOVE) into a 'processing' list solve?

options.text: It makes list reads O(1)
It prevents losing an in-flight job if the worker crashes before finishing
It compresses the list to save memory
It sorts the list by value

questions.explanation: Atomically moving a job from 'pending' to 'processing' means a crashed worker's job still sits in the processing list and can be recovered, rather than being lost as a plain LPOP would.
